# Who Has the Power? Assignments, Paste-Ready

**Generated by `scripts/build-canvas-events.js`. Do not hand-edit.**
The overview, the questions and the success criteria are the same text the
online lesson shows, read out of the content module rather than retyped, so a student
cannot be assessed against a criterion they were never shown.

Topics with no entry here are done on paper and deliberately have no Canvas
assignment. A gradebook row nobody can submit to reads as missing work for the
whole class.

## Settings, the same for every one

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Submission type | Online, then **Text Entry** |
| Attempts | Unlimited |
| Display grade as | Points |
| Peer review | Off |
| Anonymous grading | **Off** |

**Text Entry is required, not a default.** `scripts/parse-canvas-submissions.js`
reads the HTML body of a Text Entry submission. A file upload cannot be parsed
and will not appear in any analysis. **Anonymous grading must stay off**: it
suppresses the student name the parser uses, and the result is a run of
unattributable rows in `exceptions.csv`.

## WP1 - What Midterms Change

**Assignment name, Canvas and PowerSchool, character for character:** `WP1 - What Midterms Change`  
**Points:** 20  
**Calendar event it belongs to:** `CE - WP1 - The Election Nobody Understands`  

Paste the block below through the RCE **`</>`** HTML editor, never the visual one.

```html
<h2>Who Has the Power?, Topic 1: The Election Nobody Understands</h2>
<p>Find out what is on the 2026 ballot, compare the House and Senate, and explain how Congress can change while the president stays in office.</p>
<h3>Step 1 &mdash; Open the civics investigation</h3>
<p><a class="inline_disabled" href="https://jeffandersonlogic.github.io/BeCurrent/midterms/block-01.html" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Open Topic 1</a></p>
<h3>Step 2 &mdash; Watch, investigate, and explain</h3>
<p>Use the two core clips, background supports, and five-item practice. Then complete these three short responses:</p>
<ol><li>Name one verified fact about the 2026 election and one outcome still unknown. Name your source.</li><li>If House control changes, explain one thing that could change and one thing that would not automatically change.</li><li>If the president is not on the ballot, why can the midterms still change who has power? Use one verified fact.</li></ol>
<p>Each response has Start here and Push further support. Political preferences are not scored.</p>
<h3>Step 3 &mdash; Gather and submit before lunch</h3>
<p>Choose <strong>Gather All My Work</strong>. Paste into this Canvas Text Entry and submit. If copying is blocked, use the manual-copy box. Saving a draft on BeCurrent is not submission.</p>
<h3>Success criteria</h3><ol><li>I can identify congressional offices on the ballot and explain that the presidency is not being elected.</li><li>I can sort at least four of five House/Senate facts correctly and correct my errors.</li><li>I can use one verified fact to explain a possible governing consequence.</li></ol>

<p>After lunch: CNN10 and daily reporting through The Desk.</p>
```

## WP2 - The Battle for Congress

**Assignment name, Canvas and PowerSchool, character for character:** `WP2 - The Battle for Congress`  
**Points:** 20  
**Calendar event it belongs to:** `CE - WP2 - The Battle for Congress`  

Paste the block below through the RCE **`</>`** HTML editor, never the visual one.

```html
<h2>Who Has the Power?, Topic 2: The Battle for Congress</h2>
<p>Follow individual seats to chamber control. Test how a small shift can change leaders, committees, and the agenda without guaranteeing a new law.</p>
<h3>Step 1 &mdash; Open the civics investigation</h3>
<p><a class="inline_disabled" href="https://jeffandersonlogic.github.io/BeCurrent/midterms/block-02.html" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Open Topic 2</a></p>
<h3>Step 2 &mdash; Watch, investigate, and explain</h3>
<p>Use the two core clips, background supports, and five-item practice. Then complete these three short responses:</p>
<ol><li>Explain one way committee leadership can affect what Congress considers. Name your video or official source.</li><li>In the 217-to-218 scenario, what could change and why is the promised law not guaranteed?</li><li>Why can a small seat change have a large effect on congressional priorities? Include one fact and one limit.</li></ol>
<p>Each response has Start here and Push further support. Political preferences are not scored.</p>
<h3>Step 3 &mdash; Gather and submit before lunch</h3>
<p>Choose <strong>Gather All My Work</strong>. Paste into this Canvas Text Entry and submit. If copying is blocked, use the manual-copy box. Saving a draft on BeCurrent is not submission.</p>
<h3>Success criteria</h3><ol><li>I can identify the majority in a constructed 435-seat House scenario.</li><li>I can identify two decisions a new majority could influence.</li><li>I can explain one reason chamber control does not guarantee a policy change.</li></ol>

<p>After lunch: CNN10 and daily reporting through The Desk.</p>
```

<h2>Who Has the Power?, Topic 3: The Power to Stop a President</h2>

<h3>Step 1 &mdash; Open the civics investigation</h3>

<ol><li>Explain two congressional checks on the president. Identify your source.</li><li>Explain the strongest accountability argument and the strongest concern about delay in the spending scenario.</li><li>Can divided government improve accountability and make governing harder at the same time? Use one institutional example.</li></ol>
<p>Each response has Start here and Push further support. Political preferences are not scored.</p>
<h3>Step 3 &mdash; Gather and submit before lunch</h3>

<h2>Who Has the Power?, Topic 4: The Fight for Your Vote</h2>

<h3>Step 1 &mdash; Open the civics investigation</h3>

<ol><li>Choose a constructed message. Identify its claim, audience, and a detail you would check.</li><li>Record a real election claim and its source/date/link. Name an independent source you checked and explain what the evidence establishes or leaves unresolved.</li><li>Why do a favorable poll and an appealing promise fail to prove an election victory or a policy change?</li></ol>

## WP5 - Results and Impact

**Assignment name, Canvas and PowerSchool, character for character:** `WP5 - Results and Impact`  
**Points:** 30  
**Calendar event it belongs to:** `CE - WP5 - Election Night: What Happens Next?`  

Paste the block below through the RCE **`</>`** HTML editor, never the visual one.

```html
<h2>Who Has the Power?, Topic 5: Election Night: What Happens Next?</h2>
<p>Return after November 3 to record sourced 2026 results, identify unresolved races, and explain their possible governing effects. Separate established outcomes from predictions.</p>
<h3>Step 1 &mdash; Open the civics investigation</h3>
<p><a class="inline_disabled" href="https://jeffandersonlogic.github.io/BeCurrent/midterms/block-05.html" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Open Topic 5</a></p>
<h3>Step 2 &mdash; Watch, investigate, and explain</h3>
<p>Use the two core clips, background supports, and five-item practice. Then complete these three short responses and the dated results notebook:</p>
<ol><li>What do two sources establish about the results, and what remains unresolved? Compare the reporting stages.</li><li>Explain two possible governing effects of the verified outcome and one change not guaranteed. State conditions if control remains unresolved.</li><li>How did the 2026 midterms change who has power, and what could that mean? Use two identified sources, a competing interpretation, and an uncertainty.</li></ol>
<p>Each response has Start here and Push further support. Political preferences are not scored.</p>
<h3>Step 3 &mdash; Gather and submit before lunch</h3>
<p>Choose <strong>Gather All My Work</strong>. Paste into this Canvas Text Entry and submit. If copying is blocked, use the manual-copy box. Saving a draft on BeCurrent is not submission.</p>
<h3>Success criteria</h3><ol><li>I can record House, Senate, and one Indiana result or unresolved race with sources, reporting stage, and a check date.</li><li>I can explain two possible governing effects and one outcome that is not guaranteed.</li><li>I can use two identified sources, address a competing interpretation, and state an uncertainty.</li></ol>
<p>Complete after November 3, using sourced 2026 outcomes. Keep unresolved races unresolved; do not invent winners.</p>
<p>After lunch: CNN10 and daily reporting through The Desk.</p>
```
